4. Brief facts of the case are as under:-
4.1.
The original complainant, Respondent No. 2, lodged a complaint being FIR No.I-18 of 2010 under Sections 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, and 114-B of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
A chargesheet is filed against 57 accused, including the petitioner's son.
Investigating Officer recovered, Rs. 8 lakhs from the petitioner.
Petitioner filed an application under Section 451 of the Cr.P.C. (Exh. 155) for the return of muddamal i.e. the amount of Rs.8 lakhs.

Respondent No. 2 also filed a similar application (Exh.
100) for taking back said amount.
The Chief Judicial Magistrate, Surat, rejected the petitioner's application and allowed Respondent No. 2's application.

The petitioner subsequently filed Criminal Revision Application No. 464 of NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/3707/2015 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined 2011 before the learned Sessions Court, Surat which came to be rejected.

sentences.text: 5. Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that Respondent No. 2 lodged a complaint for the offenses punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, and 114-B of the Indian Penal Code against the son of the present applicant, as well as against other accused.
The Investigating Officer recovered Rs. 8,00,000/- from the applicant's bank account.

It was averred by petitioner that the applicant has a bank account in ICICI Bank, Adajan Branch, and was forced to sign a cheque and compelled to withdraw Rs. 8,00,000/- from his bank account on 26.08.2010.
The said amount was taken into possession by the Income Tax Department.
It is submitted that amount recovered by Investigating Authority was the loan amount taken by petitioner from the Bank.
5.1. It is submitted that the alleged fraud amounts to Rs. 47,50,000/-, whereas the DCB Police Station has recovered Rs. 69,00,000/-.

It is further submitted that the aforesaid amount of NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/3707/2015 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined Rs. 8,00,000/- is in no way connected to the alleged offense mentioned in the complaint.
5.2. It is submitted that the applicant is the rightful owner of the amount, and the amount which has been recovered should be returned to the applicant.
The application was rejected by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, against which the applicant filed a Criminal Revision Application.

This too was dismissed by the learned 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Surat, on 30.03.2015.
5.3.
It is submitted that the alleged offense was committed by the son of the applicant, and the applicant is in no way involved in the said offense.

The Investigating Officer has recovered Rs.
69,00,000/- in connection with the alleged fraud of Rs. 47,50,000/-.
Therefore, the amount should be returned to the applicant.

6. On the other hand, learned advocate Mr. Nikunt Raval, representing Respondent No. 2,
submitted that the statement of accused No. 1 was recorded under Section 131 of the Income NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/3707/2015 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined Tax Act, 1961 in which accused No. 1 admitted that the cheque was deposited in the said account and the amount was withdrawn from the bank account.

This clearly indicates that the account in question was being Rajkishor Santhcharan Paikarai vs State Of Gujarat on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147736706/
2 operated by both father and son.

sentences.text: The amount recovered during the search and seizure cannot be returned to the applicant until the trial is complete.
6.1. It is therefore submitted that both the Courts below have concurrently held that muddamal amount is directed to be retained by the department till the trial is concluded.

7. Learned APP Ms. Monali Bhatt, representing the respondent-State, submitted that pursuant to FIR No. I-18 of 2010, a charge-sheet has been filed, and as per the Investigation Report dated 10.10.2024, which is placed on record (and taken on record), indicates that accused No.1 and other accused are involved in offenses punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, and 114-B of the Indian Penal Code.

In view of this fact, learned APP submitted that the impugned order is in consonance with the law and no interference is required.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/3707/2015 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined 8.
I have considered the submissions and the papers placed on record.

Respondent No. 2 lodged a complaint, CR No. I-18 of 2010, before the DCB Police Station for offenses punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, and 114-B of the Indian Penal Code against 57 accused, one of whom is the son of the present applicant, who is involved in the serious offense of misappropriation of funds.

The statement recorded by the Income Tax Department under Section 131 of the Income Tax Act shows that the accused has admitted of using the account by depositing cheques and withdrawing money from the bank.

The learned Sessions Court observed that during the investigation, the offense pertaining to misappropriation and forgery of blank refund cheques amounting to Rs. 69,00,000/- was recovered by the Investigating Agency.
The findings of fact by the learned Sessions Court also indicate that a seizable amount of money was deposited by accused in his father's account, i.e., the applicant's account.

8.1. When, prima facie, it appears from the record that the applicant's account was being used by the accused in the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/3707/2015 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined process of committing the offense, it would not be appropriate at this stage to allow the applicant to claim the amount of Rs. 8,00,000/-.
9. Resultantly, I do not find any reason to interfere with the findings of the courts below in rejecting the applicant's application.
In view of this, the present application is rejected.
Rule is discharged.
